title: How access to cancer treatment has been sped up elsewhere

items.text: A peer-reviewed Nordic comparison found that patients with lung symptoms wait longer in Finland at every stage of the pathway. Elsewhere, CT is used more widely early in the pathway, which allows earlier diagnosis.

sources.title: University of Helsinki: study in Acta Oncologica 2025

items.text: Denmark introduced national cancer patient pathways in 2008, with maximum time limits for diagnostics and the start of treatment. Waiting times fell significantly.
Sweden adopted the model in 2015 (standardised care pathways, SVF). The time from well-founded suspicion to treatment is measured the same way across the country.

sources.title: Regional Cancer Centres: Cancer Patient Pathways

items.text: Swedish state funding to regions is tied to targets: 70% of patients assessed through a pathway, and 80% of those assessments completed within the target time.
England introduced a 28-day standard in 2021: cancer is diagnosed or ruled out within 28 days of referral, supported by rapid diagnostic centres.
Rapid diagnostic centres are based on the Danish model and serve patients with vague symptoms. In an evaluation, 7% were diagnosed with cancer and a third with another significant condition.
